verdict: Essentially nothing fresh is left. Every NASA-published SIBAL concurrent burn with imagery in PSI-25, PSI-26, PSI-98, PSI-99 and PSI-100 is already partitioned and scored, already tracked and compared with D1 (PSI-26 2012 stills), or already spent by the registered Saffire transfer look (docs/wsp/SAFFIRE_TRANSFER.md). Two PSI-25 SIBAL burns were never scored by any release: T13 and T20. Neither is an independent test. T13 is on a train day (GMT 100, the day of T5/T6/T16) and T20 on a validation day (GMT 190, the day of T19/T21/T22). The investigators' Table 7.1, already transcribed in docs/wsp/research/bass_published_burns.json, gives an end-state comment for both. Only the tip forecast is unseen. The batch is therefore a 2-burn tip-only check inside sessions already used, not a fresh test partition.
rule: Eligible: a burn of a NASA solid flame-spread investigation whose sample label names SIBAL and whose flow is concurrent (the only domain where D1 gives a tip forecast), with imagery in the PSI listing, that no release has scored and no track of which has been compared with D1. Grouped by GMT day (the project's BASS group key). Each burn carries the partition its day already has, because a day cannot be in two partitions. Questions whose outcome is already in the repository are excluded per burn.
